integration_issues.issue: CRITICAL REGRESSION introduced by the useStacks extraction: doUndo/doRedo call entry.undo()/entry.redo() INSIDE the setState updater function. Under React.StrictMode (enabled in src/index.js) React double-invokes updaters, so every undo/redo fires its API calls twice. Measured via network interception: add batch = 1 POST; click undo-btn = 2x DELETE /api/batches; click redo-btn = 2x POST /api/batches -> batch count went 16 -> 17 -> 16 -> 18 with TWO duplicate 'TEST_QA NET BATCH' cards. Also reproduced for the destructive-undo path: deleting a batch then clicking undo re-created the batch TWICE and duplicated its student (2x 'TEST_QA DupKid' rows) - this is a real DATA-DUPLICATION risk on the live 630-student dataset because removeBatch/removeStudent undo loops over createStudent/createPayment. Undo of an add/payment happens to look correct only because DELETE is idempotent (still 2 DELETE requests observed).

action_items: HIGH: Fix /app/frontend/src/lib/useStacks.js - move the side effect out of the setState updater. e.g. const doUndo = useCallback(async () => { const entry = undoStack[undoStack.length-1]; if (!entry) return; setUndoStack(p => p.slice(0,-1)); setRedoStack(p => [...p, entry].slice(-MAX_STACK)); await entry.undo(); await refresh(); }, [undoStack, refresh]);  (same shape for doRedo). Updaters passed to setState MUST be pure - StrictMode double-invokes them.
After the fix, re-verify: add batch -> undo (exactly 1 DELETE) -> redo (exactly 1 POST, exactly 1 card); and delete-batch -> undo restores exactly one batch + one copy of each student/payment.
critical_code_review_comments: useStacks.js doUndo/doRedo perform impure side effects (network calls) inside setUndoStack/setRedoStack updaters -> double execution under StrictMode. This is the single defect of this refactor and it can duplicate real data.

rca_of_the_issue: Root cause: /app/frontend/src/lib/useStacks.js performs network side effects inside React state updater callbacks (entry.undo()/entry.redo() are invoked within setUndoStack/setRedoStack updaters). src/index.js wraps the app in React.StrictMode, and React 18 intentionally double-invokes state updater functions to surface impurity, so each undo/redo issues its API call twice. Reproduction: /batches -> add-batch-btn -> save (1 POST) -> undo-btn (2 DELETE) -> redo-btn (2 POST, 2 duplicate cards). Impact: undo of 'Delete batch'/'Delete student' re-creates the batch/student and all its payments twice, duplicating real records; redo of add/payment duplicates records. Mitigation: read the top stack entry from state, update both stacks with pure updaters, then await the side effect outside the updater.
